svg.text: Koperasi Kegelapan — NFC Card Memory Layout
NTAG215 (504 bytes usable) · Dense Byte Assignment & Rationale
496 bytes (CARD_SIZE) = Buffer A (216B) + Buffer B (216B) + Trailer (64B)
Magic: 0x4B4F5057 ("KOPW") · Schema Version: 4 · All integers: Little-Endian · Strings: UTF-8 null-padded
• Buffer A (bytes 0–215) and Buffer B (bytes 216–431) hold identical structure — only ONE is "active" at a time (trailer.activePtr selects it)
• On write: update INACTIVE buffer → flip activePtr → ensures card is never in a half-written corrupt state (power-loss safe)
Full Card Memory Map (496 bytes total)
Each buffer (A or B) contains 5 sections — offsets are relative to buffer start
Fast rejection of non-system cards; prevents accidental decode of foreign NDEF
Schema evolution — decoder can handle old/new layouts gracefully
Future expansion: staff card, visitor pass, multi-purpose card types
Logical card identity independent from NFC UID — survives card replacement/cloning
Multi-tenant isolation — cards bound to a single koperasi branch, rejects cross-tenant reads
💡 16 bytes is 4 NTAG215 pages — minimal overhead, fits in a single NFC read command for fast validation
Member personal data (on-card for offline display)
Scout kiosk displays name without server lookup — critical for offline UX
8-char alphanumeric links to backend user — compact yet collision-resistant (62⁸ ≈ 218T)
On-card block flag — gate/terminal can reject without DB lookup (instant offline block)
Issuance audit — detects cloned cards with mismatched timestamps vs server record
💡 Bytes 50–51 reserved (2B padding for alignment). 48 bytes = 12 pages — one contiguous NFC read burst
Current balance in Rupiah — uint32 supports far beyond 16M business limit
Tamper detection — balance delta must match last log entry amount
Replay protection — server rejects if counter ≤ last seen; uint64 = never overflows
Time-order validation — rejects backdated transactions (anti-replay complement)
State machine: IDLE→CHECKED_IN→STATION_OP→CHECKED_OUT — enforces flow at gate/terminal
Future: VIP flag, discount tier, special access — no schema bump needed
💡 24 bytes = 6 pages. Intentionally compact — debit/credit operations write only this section + trailer (fast NFC write)
Parking fee calculation: ceil((endTime - startTime) / 3600) × Rp 2.000
Stored on card for receipt display — terminal shows duration without server call
Audit trail — which terminal processed this session (fraud investigation)
💡 Bytes 100–103: 4B reserved padding. 16 bytes = 4 pages — session data is zeroed on checkout complete
When the transaction happened — supports offline history display on scout kiosk
3 bytes saves 1B per entry vs uint32 — max single tx is 2M anyway (business rule)
Chain verification — each entry's balanceAfter must equal next entry's (balanceAfter ± amount)
Distinguishes credit/debit/checkin/checkout/admin ops in the log ring
Hash chain integrity — each entry's hash = SHA256(prev_hash + entry_data)[0:4]; all-zero = empty slot
💡 5 entries × 16B = 80B. Remaining buffer space (bytes 184–215) = 32B reserved for future log expansion or metadata
TRAILER — 64 bytes (offset 432–495 in full card, or byte 216–279 in wire format)
Card expiration — gate rejects expired cards offline without server check
Key rotation — stations know which AES key to use for decrypt; enables seamless key rollover
Alignment padding — keeps rootHash on 8-byte boundary for efficient reads
Fast buffer integrity check — server compares without full decrypt to detect corruption
Future use — could hold flags or additional checksum bits
HMAC includes counterBind → prevents replay of old signed trailers on new buffer data
Tamper seal — covers entire buffer + trailer anchors; 8 bytes = 2⁶⁴ brute-force resistance
Selects which buffer is current — flip after successful write for atomic update guarantee
💡 Bytes 29–63 (35B) unused — reserved for future crypto extensions. 64B trailer = 16 pages; written last for atomic commit
Total: 496 bytes used of 504 available — 98.4% utilization · AES-256-GCM encrypted body · HMAC-SHA256 signed trailer
Security: Body encrypted per-session key (from SessionGrant) · Trailer signed with tenant HMAC key · Counter monotonic · Dual-buffer atomic writes
Koperasi Kegelapan · KK Wallet · NFC Dompet Koperasi · Schema v4
